::: {.panel title="Word bank · 词库"}
**Government:** {{< vocab "republic" zh=true >}} · {{< vocab "senate" zh=true >}} · {{< vocab "consul" zh=true >}} · {{< vocab "emperor" zh=true >}} · {{< vocab "empire" zh=true >}}
**Army:** {{< vocab "legion" zh=true >}}
:::

## 1. Sort the facts

Read the ten facts. Then write each letter in the right box.

::: side-by-side
::: {}
**A.** Two consuls lead for one year.
**B.** Augustus rules for life.
**C.** Citizens elect their leaders.
**D.** The ruler's face is on every coin.
**E.** Romans have just removed their last king.
:::
::: {}
**F.** About 200 years of peace, the *Pax Romana*.
**G.** No one person may hold all the power.
**H.** The Colosseum is finished in AD 80.
**I.** Julius Caesar is a general.
**J.** The western half falls in AD 476.
:::
:::

**Republic 共和国** (509–27 BC): {{< blank 5cm answer="A, C, E, G, I" >}}    **Empire 帝国** (27 BC – AD 476): {{< blank 5cm answer="B, D, F, H, J" >}}

## 2. Put them in order

Number the events from 1 (first) to 5 (last).

::: {.sequence order="3,1,5,2,4"}
- Augustus becomes the first emperor.
- Rome becomes a republic.
- The western empire falls.
- Julius Caesar is killed.
- The Colosseum is finished.
:::

## 3. Explain the change

::: {.recall lines="4"}
- Why did some Romans want to keep the republic, even when an emperor brought peace? Start: *Some Romans wanted to keep the republic because …* | Citizens lost their vote; one person held all the power, and a bad emperor couldn't be replaced.
:::
